passages.text: These are the nations that the LORD left to test all the Israelites who had not known any of the wars in Canaan, if only to teach warfare to the subsequent generations of Israel, especially to those who had not known it formerly: the five rulers of the Philistines, all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites who lived in the mountains of Lebanon from Mount Baal-hermon to Lebo-hamath.
passages.sermon:
The LORD left certain nations in the land.
He did this to test the Israelites.
He tested those Israelites who had not experienced the wars in Canaan.
The LORD wanted to teach warfare to the later generations of Israel.
These later generations had not known war before.
The nations the LORD left were these:
The five rulers of the Philistines.
All the Canaanites.
The Sidonians.
The Hivites who lived in the mountains of Lebanon.
These Hivites lived from Mount Baal-hermon to Lebo-hamath.
passages.original: וְאֵ֤לֶּה הַגּוֹיִם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִנִּ֣יחַ יְהוָ֔ה לְנַסּ֥וֹת בָּ֖ם אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֵ֚ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־ יָדְע֔וּ אֵ֖ת כָּל־ מִלְחֲמ֥וֹת כְּנָֽעַן׃ רַ֗ק לְמַ֙עַן֙ דַּ֚עַת דֹּר֣וֹת בְּנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לְלַמְּדָ֖ם מִלְחָמָ֑ה רַ֥ק אֲשֶׁר־ לְפָנִ֖ים לֹ֥א יְדָעֽוּם׃ חֲמֵ֣שֶׁת׀ סַרְנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים וְכָל־ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִי֙ וְהַצִּ֣ידֹנִ֔י וְהַ֣חִוִּ֔י יֹשֵׁ֖ב הַ֣ר הַלְּבָנ֑וֹן מֵהַר֙ בַּ֣עַל חֶרְמ֔וֹן עַ֖ד לְב֥וֹא חֲמָֽת׃

passages.text: These nations were left to test the Israelites, to find out whether they would keep the commandments of the LORD, which He had given their fathers through Moses.
passages.sermon:
The LORD left certain nations in the land.
The LORD did this to test the Israelites.
The LORD wanted to know if the Israelites would obey His commandments.
The LORD had given these commandments to their ancestors.
The LORD gave these commandments through Moses.
passages.original: וַֽיִּהְי֕וּ לְנַסּ֥וֹת בָּ֖ם אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לָדַ֗עַת הֲיִשְׁמְעוּ֙ אֶת־ מִצְוֺ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־ צִוָּ֥ה אֶת־ אֲבוֹתָ֖ם בְּיַד־ מֹשֶֽׁה׃

passages.text: Thus the Israelites continued to live among the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites lived among other nations.
These nations included the Canaanites.
They also included the Hittites.
They included the Amorites.
They included the Perizzites.
They included the Hivites.
They included the Jebusites.
passages.original: וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל יָשְׁב֖וּ בְּקֶ֣רֶב הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֑י הַחִתִּ֤י וְהָֽאֱמֹרִי֙ וְהַפְּרִזִּ֔י וְהַחִוִּ֖י וְהַיְבוּסִֽי׃

passages.text: And they took the daughters of these people in marriage, gave their own daughters to their sons, and served their gods.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites lived among the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
The Israelites took the daughters of these nations as wives for themselves.
The Israelites gave their own daughters to the sons of these nations.
The Israelites served the gods of these nations.
passages.original: וַיִּקְח֨וּ אֶת־ בְּנוֹתֵיהֶ֤ם לָהֶם֙ לְנָשִׁ֔ים וְאֶת־ בְּנוֹתֵיהֶ֖ם נָתְנ֣וּ לִבְנֵיהֶ֑ם וַיַּעַבְד֖וּ אֶת־ אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם׃פ

passages.text: So the Israelites did evil in the sight of the LORD; they forgot the LORD their God and served the Baals and the Asherahs.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites did evil.
The LORD saw their evil.
The Israelites forgot the LORD.
The LORD was their God.
The Israelites served the Baals.
The Israelites served the Asherahs.
passages.original: וַיַּעֲשׂ֨וּ בְנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל אֶת־ הָרַע֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וַֽיִּשְׁכְּח֖וּ אֶת־ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיהֶ֑ם וַיַּעַבְד֥וּ אֶת־ הַבְּעָלִ֖ים וְאֶת־ הָאֲשֵׁרֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Then the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He sold them into the hand of Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram-naharaim, and the Israelites served him eight years.
passages.sermon:
The LORD became very angry with Israel.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
He punished Israel.
He gave Israel into the power of Cushan-rishathaim.
Cushan-rishathaim was the king of Aram-naharaim.
The Israelites served Cushan-rishathaim.
They served him for eight years.
passages.original: וַיִּֽחַר־ אַ֤ף יְהוָה֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַֽיִּמְכְּרֵ֗ם בְּיַד֙ כּוּשַׁ֣ן רִשְׁעָתַ֔יִם מֶ֖לֶךְ אֲרַ֣ם נַהֲרָ֑יִם וַיַּעַבְד֧וּ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶת־ כּוּשַׁ֥ן רִשְׁעָתַ֖יִם שְׁמֹנֶ֥ה שָׁנִֽים׃

passages.text: But when the Israelites cried out to the LORD, He raised up Othniel son of Caleb’s younger brother Kenaz as a deliverer to save them.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites suffered under foreign rule.
They cried out to the LORD for help.
The LORD heard the Israelites.
The LORD acted to save them.
The LORD chose a deliverer for Israel.
This deliverer was Othniel.
Othniel was the son of Kenaz.
Kenaz was the younger brother of Caleb.
The LORD sent Othniel to rescue the Israelites.
passages.original: וַיִּזְעֲק֤וּ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶל־ יְהוָ֔ה וַיָּ֨קֶם יְהוָ֥ה מוֹשִׁ֛יעַ לִבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וַיּֽוֹשִׁיעֵ֑ם אֵ֚ת עָתְנִיאֵ֣ל בֶּן־ קְנַ֔ז אֲחִ֥י כָלֵ֖ב הַקָּטֹ֥ן מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: The Spirit of the LORD came upon him, and he became Israel’s judge and went out to war. And the LORD delivered Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram into the hand of Othniel, who prevailed against him.
passages.sermon:
Othniel was the son of Kenaz.
Kenaz was the younger brother of Caleb.
Othniel became a leader in Israel.
The Spirit of the LORD came upon Othniel.
Othniel judged Israel.
Othniel went out to war.
Cushan-rishathaim was the king of Aram.
The LORD gave Cushan-rishathaim into Othniel’s hand.
Othniel defeated Cushan-rishathaim.
passages.original: וַתְּהִ֨י עָלָ֥יו רֽוּחַ־ יְהוָה֮ וַיִּשְׁפֹּ֣ט אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וַיֵּצֵא֙ לַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וַיִּתֵּ֤ן יְהוָה֙ בְּיָד֔וֹ אֶת־ כּוּשַׁ֥ן רִשְׁעָתַ֖יִם מֶ֣לֶךְ אֲרָ֑ם וַתָּ֣עָז יָד֔וֹ עַ֖ל כּוּשַׁ֥ן רִשְׁעָתָֽיִם׃

passages.text: So the land had rest for forty years, until Othniel son of Kenaz died.
passages.sermon:
Othniel was the son of Kenaz.
Othniel became a deliverer for Israel.
God used Othniel to save Israel.
The land had peace for forty years.
Othniel son of Kenaz died.
passages.original: וַתִּשְׁקֹ֥ט הָאָ֖רֶץ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֑ה וַיָּ֖מָת עָתְנִיאֵ֥ל בֶּן־ קְנַֽז׃פ

passages.text: Once again the Israelites did evil in the sight of the LORD. So He gave Eglon king of Moab power over Israel, because they had done evil in the sight of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites did evil.
The LORD saw their evil.
The Israelites did evil again.
Eglon was king of Moab.
The LORD gave Eglon power over Israel.
The LORD did this because the Israelites did evil.
passages.original: וַיֹּסִ֙פוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיְחַזֵּ֨ק יְהוָ֜ה אֶת־ עֶגְל֤וֹן מֶֽלֶךְ־ מוֹאָב֙ עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עַ֛ל כִּֽי־ עָשׂ֥וּ אֶת־ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: After enlisting the Ammonites and Amalekites to join forces with him, Eglon attacked and defeated Israel, taking possession of the City of Palms.
passages.sermon:
Eglon was the king of Moab.
Eglon gathered the Ammonites.
Eglon gathered the Amalekites.
Eglon brought the Ammonites and Amalekites together to help him.
Eglon went to fight against Israel.
Eglon attacked Israel.
Eglon defeated Israel.
Eglon and his allies took the City of Palms from Israel.
passages.original: וַיֶּאֱסֹ֣ף אֵלָ֔יו אֶת־ בְּנֵ֥י עַמּ֖וֹן וַעֲמָלֵ֑ק וַיֵּ֗לֶךְ וַיַּךְ֙ אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיִּֽירְשׁ֖וּ אֶת־ עִ֥יר הַתְּמָרִֽים׃

passages.text: The Israelites served Eglon king of Moab eighteen years.
passages.sermon: The Israelites served Eglon.\r\nEglon was the king of Moab.\r\nThey served him for eighteen years.
passages.original: וַיַּעַבְד֤וּ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶת־ עֶגְל֣וֹן מֶֽלֶךְ־ מוֹאָ֔ב שְׁמוֹנֶ֥ה עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה שָׁנָֽה׃ס

passages.text: And again they cried out to the LORD, and He raised up Ehud son of Gera, a left-handed Benjamite, as their deliverer. So they sent him with tribute to Eglon king of Moab.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites suffered under Eglon, king of Moab.
They cried out to the LORD for help.
The LORD heard them.
The LORD raised up a deliverer for Israel.
This deliverer was Ehud.
Ehud was the son of Gera.
Ehud belonged to the tribe of Benjamin.
Ehud was left-handed.
The Israelites chose Ehud to bring a gift to Eglon, king of Moab.
They sent Ehud with the tribute.
passages.original: וַיִּזְעֲק֣וּ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֮ אֶל־ יְהוָה֒ וַיָּקֶם֩ יְהוָ֨ה לָהֶ֜ם מוֹשִׁ֗יעַ אֶת־ אֵה֤וּד בֶּן־ גֵּרָא֙ בֶּן־ הַיְמִינִ֔י אִ֥ישׁ אִטֵּ֖ר יַד־ יְמִינ֑וֹ וַיִּשְׁלְח֨וּ בְנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל בְּיָדוֹ֙ מִנְחָ֔ה לְעֶגְל֖וֹן מֶ֥לֶךְ מוֹאָֽב׃

passages.text: Now Ehud had made for himself a double-edged sword a cubit long. He strapped it to his right thigh under his cloak and brought the tribute to Eglon king of Moab, who was an obese man.
passages.sermon:
Ehud was a man from the tribe of Benjamin.
Ehud made a sword for himself.
The sword had two edges.
The sword was a cubit long.
Ehud strapped the sword to his right thigh.
He hid the sword under his cloak.
Ehud brought a tribute to Eglon.
Eglon was the king of Moab.
Eglon was a very obese man.
passages.original: וַיַּעַשׂ֩ ל֨וֹ אֵה֜וּד חֶ֗רֶב וְלָ֛הּ שְׁנֵ֥י פֵי֖וֹת גֹּ֣מֶד אָרְכָּ֑הּ וַיַּחְגֹּ֤ר אוֹתָהּ֙ מִתַּ֣חַת לְמַדָּ֔יו עַ֖ל יֶ֥רֶךְ יְמִינֽוֹ׃ וַיַּקְרֵב֙ אֶת־ הַמִּנְחָ֔ה לְעֶגְל֖וֹן מֶ֣לֶךְ מוֹאָ֑ב וְעֶגְל֕וֹן אִ֥ישׁ בָּרִ֖יא מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: After Ehud had finished presenting the tribute, he ushered out those who had carried it.
passages.sermon:
Ehud was a left-handed man from the tribe of Benjamin.
God raised Ehud to deliver Israel from their enemies.
Ehud brought a tribute to Eglon, the king of Moab.
Ehud finished presenting the tribute.
He sent away the people who had carried the tribute.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר כִּלָּ֔ה לְהַקְרִ֖יב אֶת־ הַמִּנְחָ֑ה וַיְשַׁלַּח֙ אֶת־ הָעָ֔ם נֹשְׂאֵ֖י הַמִּנְחָֽה׃

passages.text: But upon reaching the idols near Gilgal, he himself turned back and said, “I have a secret message for you, O king.” “Silence,” said the king, and all his attendants left him.
passages.sermon:
Ehud was an Israelite judge.
Eglon was the king of Moab.
Eglon was a very obese man.
Ehud had just delivered tribute to Eglon.
Ehud left with the others who carried the tribute.
Ehud reached the idols near Gilgal.
Ehud turned back alone.
Ehud said to Eglon, “I have a secret message for you, O king.”
Eglon said, “Silence.”
All of Eglon’s attendants left him.
passages.original: וְה֣וּא שָׁ֗ב מִן־ הַפְּסִילִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֶת־ הַגִּלְגָּ֔ל וַיֹּ֕אמֶר דְּבַר־ סֵ֥תֶר לִ֛י אֵלֶ֖יךָ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הָ֔ס וַיֵּֽצְאוּ֙ מֵֽעָלָ֔יו כָּל־ הָעֹמְדִ֖ים עָלָֽיו׃

passages.text: Then Ehud approached him while he was sitting alone in the coolness of his upper room. “I have a word from God for you,” Ehud said, and the king rose from his seat.
passages.sermon:
Ehud was a judge of Israel.
Eglon was the king of Moab.
Eglon sat alone in his cool upper room.
Ehud came to Eglon.
Ehud said, “I have a message from God for you.”
Eglon stood up from his seat.
passages.original: וְאֵה֣וּד׀ בָּ֣א אֵלָ֗יו וְהֽוּא־ יֹ֠שֵׁב בַּעֲלִיַּ֨ת הַמְּקֵרָ֤ה אֲשֶׁר־ לוֹ֙ לְבַדּ֔וֹ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵה֔וּד דְּבַר־ אֱלֹהִ֥ים לִ֖י אֵלֶ֑יךָ וַיָּ֖קָם מֵעַ֥ל הַכִּסֵּֽא׃

passages.text: And Ehud reached with his left hand, pulled the sword from his right thigh, and plunged it into Eglon’s belly.
passages.sermon:
Ehud was a judge of Israel.
Ehud stood before King Eglon of Moab.
Ehud used his left hand.
Ehud reached out with his left hand.
Ehud took the sword from his right thigh.
Ehud plunged the sword into Eglon’s belly.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח אֵהוּד֙ אֶת־ יַ֣ד שְׂמֹאל֔וֹ וַיִּקַּח֙ אֶת־ הַחֶ֔רֶב מֵעַ֖ל יֶ֣רֶךְ יְמִינ֑וֹ וַיִּתְקָעֶ֖הָ בְּבִטְנֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Even the handle sank in after the blade, and Eglon’s fat closed in over it, so that Ehud did not withdraw the sword from his belly. And Eglon’s bowels emptied.
passages.sermon:
Ehud was a judge of Israel.
Eglon was the king of Moab.
Ehud attacked Eglon with a sword.
The blade of the sword went into Eglon's belly.
The handle also went in after the blade.
Eglon was a very fat man.
His fat closed over the blade and the handle.
Ehud did not pull the sword out of Eglon's belly.
Eglon's bowels emptied.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֨א גַֽם־ הַנִּצָּ֜ב אַחַ֣ר הַלַּ֗הַב וַיִּסְגֹּ֤ר הַחֵ֙לֶב֙ בְּעַ֣ד הַלַּ֔הַב כִּ֣י לֹ֥א שָׁלַ֛ף הַחֶ֖רֶב מִבִּטְנ֑וֹ וַיֵּצֵ֖א הַֽפַּרְשְׁדֹֽנָה׃

passages.text: Then Ehud went out through the porch, closing and locking the doors of the upper room behind him.
passages.sermon:
Ehud was a judge of Israel.
Ehud had just killed Eglon, the king of Moab, in the upper room.
Ehud left the upper room through the porch.
He closed the doors of the upper room behind him.
He locked the doors.
passages.original: וַיֵּצֵ֥א אֵה֖וּד הַֽמִּסְדְּר֑וֹנָה וַיִּסְגֹּ֞ר דַּלְת֧וֹת הָעַלִיָּ֛ה בַּעֲד֖וֹ וְנָעָֽל׃

passages.text: After Ehud was gone, Eglon’s servants came in and found the doors of the upper room locked. “He must be relieving himself in the cool room,” they said.
passages.sermon:
Ehud left the room.
Eglon was the king of Moab.
Eglon’s servants entered after Ehud left.
The servants saw the doors of the upper room.
The doors were locked.
The servants said, “He must be relieving himself in the cool room.”
passages.original: וְה֤וּא יָצָא֙ וַעֲבָדָ֣יו בָּ֔אוּ וַיִּרְא֕וּ וְהִנֵּ֛ה דַּלְת֥וֹת הָעֲלִיָּ֖ה נְעֻל֑וֹת וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ אַ֣ךְ מֵסִ֥יךְ ה֛וּא אֶת־ רַגְלָ֖יו בַּחֲדַ֥ר הַמְּקֵרָֽה׃

passages.text: So they waited until they became worried and saw that he had still not opened the doors of the upper room. Then they took the key and opened the doors—and there was their lord lying dead on the floor.
passages.sermon:
Eglon’s servants waited for a long time.
They became worried.
They saw that Eglon had not opened the doors of the upper room.
They took the key.
They opened the doors.
They saw their lord Eglon lying dead on the floor.
passages.original: וַיָּחִ֣ילוּ עַד־ בּ֔וֹשׁ וְהְנֵּ֛ה אֵינֶ֥נּוּ פֹתֵ֖חַ דַּלְת֣וֹת הָֽעֲלִיָּ֑ה וַיִּקְח֤וּ אֶת־ הַמַּפְתֵּ֙חַ֙ וַיִּפְתָּ֔חוּ וְהִנֵּה֙ אֲדֹ֣נֵיהֶ֔ם נֹפֵ֥ל אַ֖רְצָה מֵֽת׃

passages.text: Ehud, however, had escaped while the servants waited. He passed by the idols and escaped to Seirah.
passages.sermon:
Ehud was an Israelite judge.
Ehud escaped from the palace.
The servants waited and did not notice him leaving.
Ehud passed by the idols safely.
Ehud reached the place called Seirah and escaped there.
passages.original: וְאֵה֥וּד נִמְלַ֖ט עַ֣ד הִֽתְמַהְמְהָ֑ם וְהוּא֙ עָבַ֣ר אֶת־ הַפְּסִילִ֔ים וַיִּמָּלֵ֖ט הַשְּׂעִירָֽתָה׃

passages.text: On arriving in Seirah, he blew the ram’s horn throughout the hill country of Ephraim. The Israelites came down with him from the hills, and he became their leader.
passages.sermon:
Ehud was a judge of Israel.
Ehud arrived in Seirah.
He blew a ram’s horn in the hill country of Ephraim.
The Israelites heard the sound.
The Israelites came down from the hills.
They came down with Ehud.
Ehud went before them.
Ehud became their leader.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י בְּבוֹא֔וֹ וַיִּתְקַ֥ע בַּשּׁוֹפָ֖ר בְּהַ֣ר אֶפְרָ֑יִם וַיֵּרְד֨וּ עִמּ֧וֹ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל מִן־ הָהָ֖ר וְה֥וּא לִפְנֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: “Follow me,” he told them, “for the LORD has delivered your enemies the Moabites into your hand.” So they followed him down and seized the fords of the Jordan leading to Moab, and did not allow anyone to cross over.
passages.sermon:
Ehud was a judge of Israel.
Ehud spoke to the Israelites.
He said, "Follow me."
He said, "The LORD has given your enemies, the Moabites, into your hand."
The Israelites followed Ehud down from the hills.
They seized the fords of the Jordan River that led to Moab.
They did not allow anyone to cross over.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ רִדְפ֣וּ אַחֲרַ֔י כִּֽי־ נָתַ֨ן יְהוָ֧ה אֶת־ אֹיְבֵיכֶ֛ם אֶת־ מוֹאָ֖ב בְּיֶדְכֶ֑ם וַיֵּרְד֣וּ אַחֲרָ֗יו וַֽיִּלְכְּד֞וּ אֶת־ מַעְבְּר֤וֹת הַיַּרְדֵּן֙ לְמוֹאָ֔ב וְלֹֽא־ נָתְנ֥וּ אִ֖ישׁ לַעֲבֹֽר׃

passages.text: At that time they struck down about ten thousand Moabites, all robust and valiant men. Not one of them escaped.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites fought the Moabites at that time.
They killed about ten thousand Moabite men.
These Moabite men were strong and brave.
None of the Moabite men escaped.
passages.original: וַיַּכּ֨וּ אֶת־ מוֹאָ֜ב בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא כַּעֲשֶׂ֤רֶת אֲלָפִים֙ אִ֔ישׁ כָּל־ שָׁמֵ֖ן וְכָל־ אִ֣ישׁ חָ֑יִל וְלֹ֥א נִמְלַ֖ט אִֽישׁ׃

passages.text: So Moab was subdued under the hand of Israel that day, and the land had rest for eighty years.
passages.sermon:
Moab became subject to Israel that day.
Israel gained power over Moab.
The land became peaceful.
The land had rest for eighty years.
passages.original: וַתִּכָּנַ֤ע מוֹאָב֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא תַּ֖חַת יַ֣ד יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַתִּשְׁקֹ֥ט הָאָ֖רֶץ שְׁמוֹנִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה׃ס

passages.text: After Ehud came Shamgar son of Anath. And he too saved Israel, striking down six hundred Philistines with an oxgoad.
passages.sermon:
Shamgar was the son of Anath.
He came after Ehud.
Shamgar saved Israel.
He struck down six hundred Philistines.
He used an oxgoad to do this.
passages.original: וְאַחֲרָ֤יו הָיָה֙ שַׁמְגַּ֣ר בֶּן־ עֲנָ֔ת וַיַּ֤ךְ אֶת־ פְּלִשְׁתִּים֙ שֵֽׁשׁ־ מֵא֣וֹת אִ֔ישׁ בְּמַלְמַ֖ד הַבָּקָ֑ר וַיֹּ֥שַׁע גַּם־ ה֖וּא אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס
